evals.prompt: I accidentally ran git reset --hard and now my last commit seems gone. Please tell me how to recover it safely without making things worse.
evals.expected_output: A safety-first recovery procedure that inspects reflog, verifies a candidate commit, creates a rescue branch before moving refs, and warns against gc/prune during recovery.
expectations: Distinguishes local recovery from destructive reset and starts with git reflog.
Creates a rescue branch before moving any branch ref.
Warns that reflogs are local/expiring and says not to run gc or prune during recovery.

evals.prompt: I need to review exactly what my feature branch introduces compared with main. I have staged changes, unstaged changes, and an untracked test file. Which Git commands show each part and the final PR diff?
evals.expected_output: A precise status/diff inspection matrix covering staged, unstaged, HEAD, untracked, and merge-base-to-branch comparisons.
expectations: Uses git status and distinguishes git diff, git diff --cached, and git diff HEAD.
Explains that ordinary git diff does not show untracked content and gives a status or explicit-file inspection approach.
Uses git diff main...HEAD for the normal PR-introduction comparison and explains triple-dot semantics.

evals.prompt: My private feature branch is behind origin/main and has two commits already pushed to my personal branch. I want a clean history, but I must not overwrite someone else's work. Give me the inspect, rebase, range-diff, and safe push workflow.
evals.expected_output: A private-topic rebase workflow with fetch, backup ref, range-diff, explicit force-with-lease, and a lease-failure stop condition.
expectations: Fetches and inspects branch/upstream state before rebasing.
Creates a backup branch or equivalent recovery anchor and notes that rebase rewrites commit IDs.
Uses force-with-lease rather than plain force and tells the user to stop if the lease fails.

evals.prompt: A merge conflict happened, and git status says I am in the middle of a rebase. I do not know whether to use ours/theirs, continue, or abort. Show the safe resolution sequence.
evals.expected_output: A rebase-specific conflict protocol using status, unmerged-path/index-stage inspection, cautious ours/theirs explanation, staging, testing, continue/skip/abort.
expectations: Uses git status and diff/ls-files unmerged diagnostics before editing.
Warns that ours/theirs meanings can be counterintuitive during rebase.
Requires resolving, testing, staging, reviewing the cached diff, and then using rebase --continue or --abort.

evals.prompt: I am starting a repository from an existing directory. I want the first commit to contain only the application source, not build output or secrets, and I want a focused commit if one file has unrelated edits.
evals.expected_output: A new-repository workflow that establishes ignore/attribute policy, inspects status, uses explicit or patch staging, reviews the cached diff, and commits only the intended files.
expectations: Creates or verifies the repository and recommends .gitignore before staging.
Warns against blindly staging secrets/build output and uses explicit paths or git add -p.
Reviews git diff --cached and git diff --cached --check before commit.

evals.prompt: I need two branches checked out at once and one of them contains a submodule. Explain whether I should use worktrees, how to initialize/inspect the submodule, and what gets committed in the superproject.
evals.expected_output: A worktree and submodule explanation with separate-repository boundaries, commands for status/update, and the gitlink commit workflow.
expectations: Uses git worktree add/list and warns that worktrees share objects and normally cannot check out the same branch twice.
Uses git submodule update --init --recursive and status/diff inspection.
Explains that the superproject commits a submodule commit pointer, while submodule changes are committed/pushed inside the nested repository.
